title: Atlas Studio
description: Design systems and digital experiences for ambitious small teams.

sections.title: Frontend structure that stays elegant as the site grows.
sections.copy: Atlas Studio helps small teams ship editorial marketing sites with stronger hierarchy, cleaner systems, and fewer redesign spirals. The output is static, fast, and easy to extend.

panel.title: Codette patterns are built to stay reusable.
items: Plain HTML and CSS with tiny JS only when needed

sections.title: A slow-growing collection of layouts with clear input contracts.
sections.copy: The point is not to stockpile components. The point is to keep a short list of sections that solve real brochure-site problems well.

items.title: Hero Systems
items.copy: Headline-led intros with supporting proof, action clusters, and optional side panels.

items.title: Editorial Grids
items.copy: Feature groupings, asymmetric content blocks, and rhythm that survives real content.

items.title: Conversion Bands
items.copy: Clear CTA sections that feel deliberate instead of bolted onto the page.

sections.title: Keep the generator boring. Put the sophistication in the patterns.
sections.copy: The generator should mostly validate, render, and write files. That keeps the architecture stable while the pattern library grows through actual usage.
points: Each section pattern owns its markup and responsive behavior.
Themes define tokens, not content structure.
Site specs stay shallow enough for agents to edit confidently.

sections.quote: Small systems age better when they resist abstraction until reuse is obvious.

sections.title: Use this repo as the seed for repeatable static website generation.
sections.copy: The baseline is in place: site spec, patterns, theme, and static build output. Next, the pattern library can grow against real reference sites.

footer.blurb: A lightweight static site system built for agentic frontend workflows.
